items.title: Thyroid C-cell tumors
items.text: On all three labels. Barred with MTC or MEN2 history

items.title: Optic nerve (NAION)
items.text: Very rare with semaglutide, EMA, June 2025

items.title: Aspiration under anesthesia
items.text: US label warning, check before surgery or endoscopy

footnote: Source: US Wegovy and Zepbound labels, Chinese mazdutide label, JAMA Intern Med 2022, EMA (June 2025). Not directly comparable
notes: Most side effects are gastrointestinal. Each drug's figures come from its own label, from different trials, so they should not be ranked. Semaglutide 2.4 mg uses the pooled weight-loss trials on the US Wegovy label: nausea 44% against 16% on placebo, vomiting 24% against 6%, and 6.8% against 3.2% stopped for side effects. Tirzepatide 15 mg uses the US Zepbound label, pooling SURMOUNT-1 and 2: nausea 28% against 8%, and 6.7% against 3.4% stopped. Mazdutide 6 mg uses its Chinese label, from GLORY-1: nausea 50.5% and vomiting 43.1% against 5.9% and 2.9%, yet only 1.0% stopped in both groups. We could not obtain the Chinese labels for Wegovy and tirzepatide with their rates, so we use the US labels. There are four class risks. Thyroid C-cell tumors: all three labels carry a warning, and the drugs must not be used with a history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2. Gallbladder and bile duct disease: a meta-analysis of 76 randomized trials with over 100,000 patients found a relative risk of 2.29 in weight-loss trials. NAION, an optic nerve condition: the EMA concluded in June 2025 that it is a very rare side effect of semaglutide. China's adverse reaction monitoring center relayed this, but we found no Chinese label change. Aspiration under anesthesia or deep sedation is a warning on both US labels. Separately, the FDA asked in January 2026 for the suicidal ideation warning to be removed.
